title: Repeated cancellation of impeach hearings hit
summary: The House prosecution panel has questioned the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte over scheduling difficulties, pointing to the number of canceled trial hearings due to the unavailability of…

blocks.text: November 27, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte attends the House Committee on Appropriations' deliberation on the Office of the Vice President's (OVP's) proposed 2026 budget on Tuesday, Sept. 16, 2025.
The Philippine STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel has questioned the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte over scheduling difficulties, pointing to the number of canceled trial hearings due to the unavailability of its witnesses.

Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon, a member of the House impeachment prosecution panel, asked how much more time Duterte’s defense should be given to present its remaining witnesses, saying only two to three additional hearing days may be needed.
“It’s the third time they canceled the hearing. This week they canceled two days of hearing,” Ridon said.

The Senate impeachment court canceled its Nov. 26 and 27 hearings after lead defense counsel Sheila Sison informed presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero that counsel and prospective witnesses were unavailable, with the trial scheduled to resume Dec. 1.
Ridon has questioned why the defense could not produce even a small number of witnesses during the two canceled sessions despite maintaining that several individuals remained on its witness list.
“They said they have four to six witnesses. You mean, in those two days, they can’t produce even just two witnesses to present to the court?” he said.

The defense had originally requested 30 trial days to present evidence concerning four impeachment articles, but the prosecution subsequently withdrew three charges, leaving only Article II involving alleged unexplained wealth and financial disclosures.
Ridon said the time already used and the additional cancellations should be considered when assessing whether further postponements would be justified.
“I think they already consumed eight days, then they canceled three days, so it already exceeds 10 days,” he said.

The defense has insisted that adjustments to its witness schedule are necessary to ensure a fair presentation, while the impeachment court retains discretion over the hearing calendar and has not imposed Ridon’s proposed remaining-day limit.
“I think two, three days are left for them to present,” Ridon estimated, as prosecutors awaited the updated witness list and the resumption of hearings in December.

House prosecutors yesterday refuted the claims of Vice President Duterte that she enjoys high popularity ratings because Filipinos believe she is innocent of the unexplained wealth charges leveled against her.
“No (amount of) survey can erase the accountability of any high-ranking official (in government),” House Deputy Speaker Janette Garin said.
“This cannot erase the documents that have been presented by the prosecution,” she added.
Garin nevertheless acknowledged Duterte’s right to seek public sympathy, adding that her appeals to supporters do not affect the prosecution’s case.
“History will judge any official based on how they responded to allegations. If your conscience is indeed clean, then you have nothing to fear. Face the charges head on,” the lawmaker added.

Fellow prosecutor House Deputy Speaker Rep. Jefferson Khonghun of Zambales’ 1st District agreed. “This is not a popularity contest. The core issue here is: explain why the extent of your wealth reached that much, as well as the reveal source of all your assets,” he said.

The prosecution, led by Batangas 2nd District Rep. Gerville Luistro has presented an estimate of P817.87 million in alleged undeclared assets and unexplained wealth involving Duterte and her husband from 2022 to 2025. — Delon Porcalla
